title: SDK lightweight retry modes and structured output assertions PRD
content:
Context and motivation:

Teams embedding Hosted API streaming with tool-calls are seeing two recurring failure modes that impact developer UX and customer SLAs: (1) transient network blips leading to partial or duplicate tool invocations, and (2) structured-output payloads (JSON, JSONL, typed frames) that only partially materialize when the stream disconnects or when the runtime falls back to a cheaper model variant.

Goal (what success looks like):
- Developer ergonomics: SDK surfaces 3 small, composable retry modes that are trivial to opt into and to reason about for deterministic tool effects.
- Output fidelity: End-to-end guards and lightweight assertion hooks for structured outputs so clients can detect and recover from truncated/invalid payloads with minimal code.
- Observability: Telemetry events that allow us to measure per-route frequency of partial-tool failures, retry amplification, and structured-output regression rates.
- Operational safety: Default behavior for free-tier/hosted users is conservative (no automatic double-exec), enterprise customers can opt into stronger speculative retrying under SLA and can provide idempotency tokens for toollets.

Non-goals:
- This PRD is not proposing a large protocol overhaul (no new long-term wire formats). Aim is SDK-side patterns + small server-side feature flags.

Problem statements and examples:
- Example A: Mobile client uses streaming to request a multi-step tool graph (search -> call external DB -> synthesize). Network dropout at t+2s causes the client to reconnect and resubmit the same session; the DB call executes twice because the toollet runtime had insufficient idempotency metadata.
- Example B: A chat app receives a JSONL manifest describing items to render. The stream stops mid-record. The client shows a partial list and later reconciles incorrectly because the SDK accepted the truncated record as final.

Key proposals (high level):
1) SDK Retry Modes (three opt-in modes, ordered by aggressiveness):
   - none: default. SDK does not retry tool calls automatically; surface error to developer. (safest, avoids double-exec)
   - safe-replay: on reconnect/resume, SDK will replay only requests that did not receive an explicit ack from the platform. Replays are tagged with a replay-id; server uses lightweight ack logs to suppress duplicates if idempotency tokens match. This relies on server-side minimal ack logs (TTL-limited).
   - speculative: in addition to safe-replay, the client may speculatively re-invoke short-lived, idempotent toollets (e.g., scoring functions) during transient failures to reduce latency. Speculative mode requires explicit opt-in and will send an advisory header so server-side billing/telemetry separates speculative invocations.

   Implementation notes:
   - SDK surface: enum RetryMode {NONE, SAFE_REPLAY, SPECULATIVE} in major SDKs (JS/TS, Python, Go). Small helper: setSessionId(sessionId) + optional idempotencyKey per-tool-call.
   - Server-side: maintain ack index per-session with short TTL (e.g., 30s) for SAFE_REPLAY semantics; record speculative flag per-invocation.

2) Structured Output Assertions and Recovery Hooks:
   - Provide an SDK API that accepts a lightweight schema/assertion function for streamed frames. Example: onFrame(frame) -> returns {valid: bool, reason?: string}. If invalid and the session is resumable, SDK exposes a recovery strategy: request server to roll forward full object, attempt re-parse, or surface a structured-validation error to the application.
   - Prebuilt validators: JSON schema (draft-07 subset), typed-frame-check (frame id + checksum), and a small DSL for asserting presence of high-level keys.
   - Default behavior: when no validator is provided, SDK will attempt best-effort JSON parse; if parse fails mid-stream, SDK surfaces a structured-parse error and returns last stable checkpoint if available.

3) Compact handshake metadata for low-bandwidth clients:
   - A small handshake header in the initial session start that includes: session_id, preferred_retry_mode, validation_profile_id (optional). Keeps additional fields minimal for mobile.

4) Telemetry and observability:
   - New telemetry events emitted by SDK: structured_validation_failure, replay_attempt, speculative_invocation, duplicate_suppressed, truncated_frame_detected. Each event includes route/model, session_id, retry_mode, and numeric latency buckets.
   - Server emits metrics: per-route replay suppression rate, speculative-invocations-per-minute, and structured-output-failure-rate.

5) Backward compatibility and rollout strategy:
   - Phase 1 (server-side): implement ack index + speculative flagging behind a feature flag; expose telemetry. Ship minimal API changes so old SDKs continue to work (ack logs ignored).
   - Phase 2 (SDKs): ship JS/TS and Python SDKs with RetryMode enum and validators. Default is NONE. Documentation: migration guide and 3 short recipes (mobile resume pattern, desktop optimistic UX, enterprise speculative mode).
   - Phase 3 (samples and field trials): run controlled trials with several internal customers on SAFE_REPLAY. Monitor duplicate_suppressed metric and adjust ack TTLs.

Operational details and edge cases:
- Idempotency guidance: not all toollets can be safely replayed. We will provide patterns for wrapping non-idempotent external calls behind our orchestration (e.g., server-side guard that attaches external-call idempotency tokens).
- Replay amplification: if many clients reconnect concurrently, safe_replay should not cause thundering herd; server-side suppression should scale via bloom-filter style suppression window and per-session ack. We will set default per-route replay rate limits and add soft-fail response codes to clients when suppression is active.
- Speculative billing: speculative invocations are marked and exposed in billing/usage analytics so customers understand cost impact. Speculative-only invocations will be discounted in early trials.

API sketches (JS-like pseudo):
- session = Redwood.createSession({model: 'rwd-chat-v1', retryMode: RetryMode.SAFE_REPLAY, validationProfile: 'json-order-list-v1'})
- session.callTool('db-write', {payload}, {idempotencyKey: 'txn-123'})
- session.on('frame', (frame) => { let result = session.validateFrame(frame); if (!result.valid) session.requestRecovery(frame.id) })

Metrics to track (success criteria):
- Reduction in customer-visible duplicate-tool-errors (target: <= 0.02% of calls under SAFE_REPLAY in trial)
- Structured-output-consistency (fraction of streams with at least one structured-validation-failure; target < 0.5% in first month after SDK rollout)
- Telemetry coverage: >= 90% of active sessions emit at least baseline telemetry events after SDK upgrade
- No increase in median tail latency for typical streaming calls in SAFE_REPLAY mode (SLO: <= +10ms p99)

Security and privacy considerations:
- Ack logs must not contain user PII. Store only session_id, frame_ids, and hash of idempotency tokens. Retain for minimal TTL and encrypt at rest.
- Speculative invocations must be discoverable and auditable—flagging is required so customers can opt-out for regulated workloads.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Ack TTL default: 30s vs 120s. Short TTL reduces replays but could make safe_replay less useful for flaky mobile networks.
2) Speculative default availability: should speculative be enterprise-only behind SLA?
3) Validation profiles: how many built-in validators do we need at GA (3 vs 8)?
4) Billing model for speculative: full price vs discounted test pricing during trial?

Next steps and immediate action items (owner initials):
- Build server-side ack index prototype and simple suppression logic (ENG infra; owner: Miles) — due 2026-02-01
- SDK API spec for RetryMode + validator hooks (owner: Ava) — due 2026-01-29
- Telemetry event schema and Grafana boards (owner: Priya) — due 2026-02-05
- Internal field trial plan with 3 customers and instrumentation checklist (owner: Jonah) — due 2026-02-12

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally lightweight and SDK-forward. I want feedback on the safety tradeoffs (esp. ack TTL) and whether we should add a fourth, developer-friendly mode (auto-ack-then-replay) for single-shot RPC-style flows.

Appendix (examples and developer snippets):
- Example validator (JS): function orderListValidator(frame) { try { const obj = JSON.parse(frame.text); if (!Array.isArray(obj.items)) return {valid:false, reason:'items missing'}; return {valid:true} } catch (e) { return {valid:false, reason:'parse error'} } }

- Recovery flow sketch: client detects truncated_frame -> calls session.requestRecovery(frameId) -> server checks ack log -> if full object available in durable store, return full payload -> else surface structured-parse error to client.

End of doc.
